parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no documented police targeting of gender-nonconforming people, no trans violence, and police reported no incitement/toleration of violence (2023). But the morality statute is not a dead letter: prosecutions in 2022 and a December 2024 conviction with five- and six-month terms actually served show a state willing to imprison for related conduct, and the applicable penalty is unresolved. Combined with zero recourse — no gender-identity anti-discrimination law, no marker change, no functioning LGBTQ organisation, widespread impunity, documented stigmatisation and low acceptance (26% say their area is good for LGBTQ people) — an outed trans visitor faces social hostility with no remedy and a possible lever via morality or fraud-type provisions. Visitor-facing axes (borders, facilities, wards, custody) are unsourced, so they are open questions, not documented exposures; I weight them lightly. Above 0.35 because no enforced universal exposure or organised targeting reaches visitors; below 0.45 because the criminalising regime is actively enforced and entirely unremedied.
